accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Yellow Revolution is associated with oilseeds and edible oils. Blue is associated with fisheries, Silver with eggs and poultry, and Golden Fibre with jute.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure product-revolution pair and eliminate reversed commodities.
accepted.sec: Revolution → product + person; Rainbow Revolution pairs  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to agricultural revolutions in India, consider the following pairs:

a. Blue Revolution — Hiralal Chaudhuri and Arun Krishnan
b. Pink Revolution — Durgesh Patel
c. Red Revolution — Vishal Tewari
d. Golden Revolution — Nirpakh Tutej

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched in the stated classification. The Blue Revolution is linked with fisheries and aquaculture, Pink with meat processing, prawn, onion and pharmaceuticals, Red with meat and tomato, and Golden with horticulture and honey.
accepted.tq: Use the person-product association in each pair rather than relying on the colour alone.
accepted.sec: Revolution → product + person; Rainbow Revolution pairs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The term ‘Golden Fibre Revolution’ is associated with which commodity?
accepted.x: The Golden Fibre Revolution refers to jute. Cotton is associated with the Silver Fibre Revolution.
accepted.tq: Tests a confusable colour-commodity pair using a nearby commodity as the distractor.
accepted.sec: Revolution → product + person; Rainbow Revolution pairs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Technology Mission on Cotton is associated with which revolution?
accepted.x: The Silver Fibre Revolution is associated with cotton through the Technology Mission on Cotton.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact official term instead of choosing the better-known Golden Fibre association.
accepted.sec: Revolution → product + person; Rainbow Revolution pairs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Round Revolution is associated with potato, not oilseeds. Oilseeds are associated with the Yellow Revolution.
accepted.tq: Find the single commodity that belongs to another colour revolution.
accepted.sec: Revolution → product + person; Rainbow Revolution pairs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The expression ‘Rainbow Revolution’ refers to:
o: A programme limited to horticulture and honey production
Only the simultaneous growth of foodgrain and dairy production
The sequence of phases of the Green Revolution
The umbrella of colour revolutions covering crops, livestock and fisheries
accepted.x: Rainbow Revolution is the umbrella term for the different colour revolutions and represents holistic agricultural growth across crops, livestock and fisheries.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an umbrella concept from one of its component revolutions.
accepted.sec: Revolution → product + person; Rainbow Revolution pairs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Green Revolution in India began in the mid-1960s in the backdrop of which development?
o: The abolition of the Annual Plans in 1960
The completion of the Third Five-Year Plan with record foodgrain output
A decline in irrigation accompanied by a rise in foodgrain output
A sharp fall in foodgrain output after the droughts of 1965-66 and 1966-67
accepted.x: The Green Revolution began in the mid-1960s after droughts in 1965-66 and 1966-67 caused foodgrain output to fall sharply.
accepted.tq: Link the policy shift to its immediate economic trigger.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution - Plan period, phases, key persons, place of start  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Foodgrain output in India fell to approximately what levels after the droughts of 1965-66 and 1966-67, respectively?
accepted.x: Foodgrain output fell to 72.3 million tonnes in 1965-66 and 74.2 million tonnes in 1966-67.
accepted.tq: Read the paired figures in the stated chronological order.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution - Plan period, phases, key persons, place of start  [APPSC]

accepted.s: High-yielding variety seeds were adopted as a full programme during which period?
accepted.x: HYV seeds were adopted as a full programme from 1966 during the Annual Plans of 1966-69.
accepted.tq: Use the plan-period distinction to separate Annual Plans from Five-Year Plans.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution - Plan period, phases, key persons, place of start  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Agricultural growth during the Annual Plans of 1966-69, when HYV seeds were adopted as a full programme, was approximately:
accepted.x: Agricultural growth during the Annual Plans of 1966-69 was 4.16%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact percentage from nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution - Plan period, phases, key persons, place of start  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the phases of the Green Revolution given in the classification?
o: Pre-Green Revolution: 1951-68; Early phase: 1968-81; Later phase: 1987-92
Pre-Green Revolution: 1951-66; Early phase: 1966-80; Later phase: 1981-92
Pre-Green Revolution: 1956-68; Early phase: 1968-87; Later phase: 1987-95
Pre-Green Revolution: 1951-60; Early phase: 1960-75; Later phase: 1975-92
accepted.x: The stated classification identifies 1951-68 as the pre-Green Revolution period, 1968-81 as the early phase and 1987-92 as the later phase.
accepted.tq: Match each phase with its complete date range rather than only its starting year.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution - Plan period, phases, key persons, place of start  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who among the following was the Union Agriculture Minister associated with driving the policy shift towards the Green Revolution in India?
accepted.x: C. Subramaniam, as Union Agriculture Minister, drove the policy shift towards the Green Revolution. Norman Borlaug and M.S. Swaminathan had scientific roles, while Verghese Kurien was associated with the White Revolution.
accepted.tq: Separate the ministerial policy role from the scientific and dairy roles.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution - Plan period, phases, key persons, place of start  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the contribution of Norman Borlaug?
o: He founded the National Dairy Development Board.
He developed semi-dwarf wheat and is regarded as the father of the global Green Revolution.
He developed the first semi-dwarf rice variety in India.
He developed the three-tier dairy cooperative model at Anand.
accepted.x: Norman Borlaug developed semi-dwarf wheat and is regarded as the father of the global Green Revolution.
accepted.tq: Use the contribution-based distinction among scientists, administrators and dairy pioneers.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution - Plan period, phases, key persons, place of start  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Punjab is called the ‘Granary of India’ primarily because it was:
o: The pioneer state of the Green Revolution
The first state to introduce Operation Flood
The first state to establish the NDDB
The exclusive producer of Indian dwarf rice
accepted.x: Punjab was the pioneer state of the Green Revolution and is consequently called the ‘Granary of India’.
accepted.tq: Connect the title with the specific historical agricultural role stated for the state.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution - Plan period, phases, key persons, place of start  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In 1966, approximately how much Mexican wheat was imported and crossed with local varieties in Punjab?
accepted.x: In 1966, 18,000 tonnes of Mexican wheat was imported and crossed with local varieties in Punjab.
accepted.tq: Test the exact quantity while keeping the unit and year fixed.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution - Plan period, phases, key persons, place of start  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The rise in wheat production associated with the introduction of Mexican wheat varieties in Punjab was from approximately:
accepted.x: Wheat production rose from about 5 million tonnes to 17 million tonnes after the introduction and crossing of Mexican varieties.
accepted.tq: Compare the before-and-after production figures without reversing their order.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution - Plan period, phases, key persons, place of start  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a high-yielding variety or wheat selection?
o: Taichung Native-1 — First semi-dwarf rice introduced in India
Kalyan Sona — Mexican dwarf wheat developed by Borlaug
Lerma Rojo 64-A — Dwarf rice from the Philippines
accepted.x: Taichung Native-1, or TN-1, was the first semi-dwarf rice introduced in India in 1965. IR-8 was dwarf rice from IRRI, while Kalyan Sona was an Indian dwarf wheat selection and Lerma Rojo 64-A was Mexican dwarf wheat.
accepted.tq: Separate rice varieties from Mexican wheat and Indian wheat selections.
accepted.sec: HYV varieties - IR-8, first dwarf rice, Mexican wheat  [APPSC]

accepted.s: IR-8, often called ‘miracle rice’, was:
o: A dwarf rice variety from IRRI in the Philippines, associated with 1966
An Indian wheat selection resistant to lodging
The first semi-dwarf rice introduced in India in 1965 from Mexico
A variety of cotton developed under the Technology Mission on Cotton
accepted.x: IR-8 was a dwarf rice variety from the International Rice Research Institute in the Philippines and is associated with 1966.
accepted.tq: Discriminate IR-8 from TN-1 and from the wheat varieties listed alongside it.
accepted.sec: HYV varieties - IR-8, first dwarf rice, Mexican wheat  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs consists entirely of Mexican dwarf wheat varieties associated with Borlaug?
accepted.x: Lerma Rojo 64-A and Sonora 64 were Mexican dwarf wheat varieties associated with Borlaug. Kalyan Sona and Sonalika were Indian dwarf wheat selections.
accepted.tq: Group the varieties by crop origin and distinguish Mexican wheat from Indian selections.
accepted.sec: HYV varieties - IR-8, first dwarf rice, Mexican wheat  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding HYV crops is correct?
1. Their short stature helps them resist lodging.
2. They respond to fertiliser and water.
3. Their quicker maturity can permit double cropping.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. HYVs are short-statured, respond to fertiliser and water, mature faster and can therefore support double cropping.
accepted.tq: Recognise a complete set of linked agronomic characteristics rather than isolating one feature.
accepted.sec: HYV varieties - IR-8, first dwarf rice, Mexican wheat  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by which organisation?
o: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
accepted.x: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB).
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who launched the programme?’ institutional trap.
accepted.sec: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The three-tier cooperative model adopted by Operation Flood was based on the model developed at:
accepted.x: Operation Flood copied the Amul three-tier cooperative model developed at Anand in Gujarat.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the starting location of the cooperative model from the Green Revolution state.
accepted.sec: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three tiers of the Operation Flood cooperative model?
o: Village society → district union → state federation
Village society → state federation → district union
District union → village society → state federation
State federation → village society → district union
accepted.x: The three tiers proceed from the village society to the district union and then to the state federation.
accepted.tq: Arrange the institutional levels from the grassroots unit to the apex federation.
accepted.sec: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Phase I of Operation Flood:
1. It covered the period 1970-80.
2. It was financed by the World Food Programme.
3. Milk sheds in 18 states were linked to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe Phase I of Operation Flood: 1970-80, World Food Programme financing and linkage of milk sheds in 18 states to four major cities.
accepted.tq: Check the period, funding agency and achievement as three separate components.
accepted.sec: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During Phase II of Operation Flood, milk sheds increased from 18 to 136 and urban markets increased up to:
accepted.x: Phase II, covering 1981-85, increased milk sheds from 18 to 136 and expanded urban markets up to 200.
accepted.tq: Pair the phase-specific expansion figures rather than confusing them with Phase I or III.
accepted.sec: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What was the principal achievement attributed to Phase III of Operation Flood?
o: Establishing the first semi-dwarf rice research centre
Linking 18 milk sheds to four metropolitan cities
accepted.x: Phase III, covering 1985-96, added 30,000 new dairy cooperatives.
accepted.tq: Match the achievement with the correct phase and reject achievements belonging to earlier phases.
accepted.sec: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Operation Flood was associated with the dairy cooperative leadership of Verghese Kurien and:
accepted.x: Verghese Kurien worked with Tribhuvandas Patel at Anand in the development of the dairy cooperative movement.
accepted.tq: Use the associated-person trap by separating dairy pioneers from Green Revolution figures.
accepted.sec: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien  [APPSC]

accepted.s: White Revolution 2.0 was launched in September 2024 by the:
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying alone
accepted.x: White Revolution 2.0 was launched by the Ministry of Cooperation in September 2024.
accepted.tq: Apply the ministry-swap trap to a recently launched programme.
accepted.sec: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien  [APPSC]

accepted.s: White Revolution 2.0 plans to create how many new dairy cooperative societies?
accepted.x: White Revolution 2.0 plans to establish 75,000 new dairy cooperative societies.
accepted.tq: Test the programme target against nearby rounded figures.
accepted.sec: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The procurement target under White Revolution 2.0 by 2028-29 is:
accepted.x: The target is procurement of 1,007 lakh kilograms of milk per day by 2028-29.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact target and retain the lakh kg/day unit.
accepted.sec: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding India’s milk production?
o: India produced about 148 MMT in 2023-24 and is the world’s largest producer.
India produced 239.3 MMT in 2023-24 and is the world’s largest milk producer.
India’s annual output is below 200 MT and is declining steadily.
India produced 239.3 MMT in 2023-24 but ranks second in the world.
accepted.x: Milk output was 239.3 million metric tonnes in 2023-24, and India is the world’s largest milk producer.
accepted.tq: Combine the numerical figure with the comparative world-ranking fact.
accepted.sec: White Revolution - Operation Flood phases, starting state, Kurien  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The focus of the Second Green Revolution includes which of the following?
1. Pulses, oilseeds and millets
2. Precision farming using drones and artificial intelligence
3. Micro-irrigation and integrated nutrient and pest management
4. Climate-resilient varieties
accepted.x: The Second Green Revolution focuses on all the listed areas, including Shree Anna, precision technologies, resource-efficient irrigation, integrated management and climate resilience.
accepted.tq: Recognise the comprehensive objective list and use the all-inclusive option only when every item fits.
accepted.sec: Second Green Revolution / Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal objective associated with the Evergreen Revolution is to:
o: Raise productivity without causing ecological harm
Replace all foodgrains with commercial crops
Restrict agricultural growth to irrigated regions
Increase production exclusively through chemical fertilisers
accepted.x: The Evergreen Revolution seeks to raise agricultural productivity while avoiding ecological harm.
accepted.tq: Apply the sustainability principle to distinguish Evergreen Revolution from a purely output-oriented approach.
accepted.sec: Second Green Revolution / Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Prime Minister called for a Second Green Revolution?
accepted.x: Manmohan Singh called for a Second Green Revolution.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the political call for the Second Green Revolution from the scientific idea of Evergreen Revolution.
accepted.sec: Second Green Revolution / Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI) is a sub-scheme of:
accepted.x: BGREI is a sub-scheme of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY).
accepted.tq: Use the parent-scheme identification method and reject programmes from adjacent agricultural sectors.
accepted.sec: Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: BGREI has been implemented since:
accepted.x: BGREI has been implemented since 2010-11.
accepted.tq: Test the exact implementation year against adjacent agricultural programme years.
accepted.sec: Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following states is NOT included in the listed geographical coverage of BGREI?
accepted.x: The listed BGREI states are Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, eastern Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. Tamil Nadu is not included in that list.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a region-based state list.
accepted.sec: Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the aim of BGREI?
o: To shift all cotton production from western India to eastern India
To promote petroleum production through eastern industrial corridors
To establish dairy cooperatives in every eastern district
To raise rice-based productivity in eastern India through HYVs, irrigation, balanced nutrients and IPM
accepted.x: BGREI aims to raise rice-based productivity in eastern India through high-yielding varieties, irrigation, balanced nutrient use and integrated pest management.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with its crop, region and intervention package.
accepted.sec: Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The later Purvodaya idea of shifting the rice bowl eastward follows the same broad logic as:
o: Expanding rice-based productivity in eastern India
Replacing HYV seeds with traditional varieties throughout India
Concentrating agriculture only in Punjab and Haryana
accepted.x: Purvodaya follows the logic of improving rice-based productivity and shifting the rice bowl towards eastern India, as envisaged by BGREI.
accepted.tq: Recognise the continuity between a later policy idea and the earlier regional productivity strategy.
accepted.sec: Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI)  [APPSC]
